text.p: Fast bowler Glenn McGrath on Wednesday passed a fitness on his blistered heel to strengthen Australia's bowling attack for the first test against West Indies, starting on Friday.
McGrath, Australia's new ball strike bowler, emerged unscathed from a training session lasting almost three hours, Australian Cricket Board (ACB) spokesman Patrick Keane said.
"I gave it a full go and it felt great," McGrath later told reporters.
McGrath's availability bolsters an attack weakened after injuries ruled out veteran fast bowler Craig McDermott and fellow paceman Damien Fleming.
Australia are also pinning their hopes on leg-spinner Shane Warne, who is playing his first international match since surgery on the ring finger of his bowling hand in May.
Warne has only bowled sparingly in two appearances for Victoria this season and there remain doubts as to whether he will be able to bowl lengthy spells without discomfort in Brisbane.
Inexperienced fast bowlers Michael Kasprowicz and Jason Gillespie are expected to challenge for the remaining available berth in the pace attack alongside McGrath and Paul Reiffel.
